intro: Paste the trace — one real piece of work walked backwards through all six links with a name against each, the earliest weak link, and the hour where Decide and Produce happened together — followed by the 200–300 word write-up including your position on this module's claim. Resubmission is free and unlimited — the score is a mirror, not a gate.
activityContext:
You are grading a learner submission for AI 301 · The Specialist, Employee Experience / Internal Comms track. Module 2 applied activity, 'One piece of work, traced': ONE significant thing the function shipped in the last quarter, walked backwards from Verify to Sense, with what happened and who did it — by name — at each link; the earliest point at which it could have gone wrong; and one hour where Decide and Produce happened simultaneously, to the same person, with a document open.

Scope note: this module traces one artifact. Module 4 maps the whole function against the chain. A learner who submits a full function-wide map here has done Module 4's work early — credit the effort, but the trace of a single real piece is what this activity is grading, and depth on one item beats breadth across many.

The unevenness is the finding. In most functions Produce and Distribute have names attached immediately, Verify has a name only if something went wrong once before, and Sense and Decide have somebody else's name or none. A learner reporting 'no one did Sense on this' is giving the correct answer, not an incomplete one — score it at the top.

Step 4 is the module's central skill: separating counsel from artifact work inside a single hour. A learner who finds that hour and names what the Decide part actually was has understood the module. A learner who cannot find one, and explains why in a way that engages the distinction, also scores well — but 'there wasn't any' with no reasoning usually means Decide was absorbed into Produce unnoticed, and feedback should say so.

This track scores the delta rather than the score. The numeric prediction opened here (share of the week spent producing) stays OPEN — it is measured and closed in Module 4 — so do not grade it for accuracy here or anywhere. Grade accounts of gaps, never the size of them.

opening.label: Predicted — share of your team's week spent producing things
opening.hint: Drafting, editing, formatting, building decks, kits and pages. Module 4 measures this against a real instrument and closes the loop.

dimensions.name: All six links are traced, backwards, with names
dimensions.criteria: Every link addressed for one real piece of work — what happened and who did it — worked from Verify back to Sense rather than forwards from Produce. 'Nobody' is a valid and often correct answer at Sense, Decide and Verify, and should score at the top when stated plainly. A trace that covers only Produce and Distribute, without noting the others were absent, is the gap to name in feedback.

dimensions.name: The piece is real and consequential
dimensions.criteria: A genuine shipped artifact from the last quarter, aimed at the audience carried from Module 1 — a change announcement, policy rollout, or campaign rather than routine traffic. Enough specificity that the trace could not have been written about any organization. A hypothetical or a generic example cannot demonstrate what this activity is for.

dimensions.name: The earliest weak link is identified upstream of the wording
dimensions.criteria: A named first point of failure or risk, with reasoning. The move this dimension rewards is refusing the easy answer: if the piece landed badly, checking Sense, Interpret and Decide before blaming Produce. If it landed well, naming the link they'd most worry about on a repeat. 'The wording could have been clearer' with nothing upstream examined scores poorly.

dimensions.name: The Decide hour is separated from the Produce hour
dimensions.criteria: The module's central skill: one specific hour where counsel and artifact work happened together, with the Decide part named — a framing changed, a sponsor refused, an order of announcement altered, a claim removed. A reasoned account of why no such hour exists also scores well. An unexamined 'there wasn't any' does not.

dimensions.name: The position engages the sharpest counter
dimensions.criteria: A committed position on the claim that the link holding most of the team's time matters least, engaging the strongest case against it: that Produce is where quality actually lives, that the chain flatters invisible upstream work, and — the hardest version — that if AI had genuinely collapsed Produce, quality would have converged across organizations and it plainly hasn't, which suggests the floor rose while the ceiling stayed put. Agreement or disagreement both score well. Ignoring the 'floor rose, ceiling didn't' argument is the weakest form. Plus the closing sentence on who should be in the room rather than what should have been written.
